ATTRIBUTE.Name: Specimen ID
ATTRIBUTE.Description: A unique identifier of the Specimen.
ATTRIBUTE.Explanation: The uniqueness refers to the context of the dataset. Defined by the data submitter.

Value_Specification.Comment: CAVEAT: During dataset creation the submitter must use the Object Attribute “alias” to state a unique identifier, however, during the submission process that repository automatically generates a unique accession ID for each submitted CMMS Entity. This accession ID will be automatically injected into the XML file using the xs:attribute “accession” by the repository during the upload process. Once a accession ID has been generated all references to a given CMMS Entity must use the xs:attribute “accession” and not the xs:attribute “alias”.

ATTRIBUTE.Name: Extracted From
ATTRIBUTE.Description: The ID of the Biological Being the Specimen was extracted from.

Value_Specification.Comment: CAVEAT: During dataset creation the xs:attribute “alias” must be used to reference a given CMMS Entity if the given CMMS Entity has not received an accession ID by the repository yet (I.e. Non-Complementary Datasets). However, during the submission process the repository will assign unique accession IDs to every CMMS Entity and internal references will be updated using the newly generated accession IDs by injecting them into the XML files. Once an accession ID has been assigned to a given CMMS Entity the xs:attribute “accession” must be used to reference the given CMMS Entity. This especially relates to Complementary Datasets, where only the xs:attribute “accession” must be used (also during data set creation) when an accession ID exists for a given CMMS Entity.

ATTRIBUTE.Name: Age at Extraction
ATTRIBUTE.Description: The age of the Biological Being at the time point of extraction of the Specimen.
ATTRIBUTE.Explanation: Can be stratified (or even left empty) if needed to comply with GDPR anonymization requirements.

Value_Specification.NA: Allowed for clinical; not allowed for non-clinical
Value_Specification.Comment:
To allow stratified ages, the Age of Extraction is stated by means of a time interval. The interval contains two child attributes: ATTRIBUTE ID 3.2.4.1: Interval Start and ATTRIBUTE ID 3.2.4.2: Interval Length. Both the start of the interval and the length of the interval are stated in terms of the ISO-8601 Standard (Duration). The interval described by means of 'interval start' and 'interval length' is defined as a left closed and right open interval (i.e. [start, end[).
Example Age at Extraction - stratified by 10 years: The interval [50, 60[ must be encoded as follows: • interval start: P50Y, • interval length: P10Y
If an explicit age without stratification should be encoded (i.e. 50) the interval length must be stated as 'PT0S'.
Example - Age at Extraction 50 years: The interval must be encoded as follows: • interval start: P50Y, • interval length: PT0S

ATTRIBUTE.Name: Anatomical Site
ATTRIBUTE.Description: The anatomical site (here considered on an organ level, or similar concepts such as retroperitoneum if no organ is available) the Specimen originated from.
ATTRIBUTE.Explanation: A Specimen should originate from one specific anatomical site. In case tissue from different anatomical sites were derived during one extraction, a separate specimen should be created for each individual anatomical site. In cases where this is not possible one can use the attribute ATTRIBUTE ID 3.3.2 Anatomical Site List. However, this should be avoided if possible.

Value_Specification.NA: Allowed for clinical; not allowed for non-clinical
Value_Specification.Comment: SCHEMA: • SNOMED CT ‘Body structure (body structure)’ Concept and children.

ATTRIBUTE.Name: Anatomical Site List
ATTRIBUTE.Description: A list of anatomical sites (here considered on an organ level, or similar concepts such as retroperitoneum if no organ is available) the Specimen originated from. This attribute contains a set of attributes of ATTRIBUTE ID 3.3.1: Anatomical Site.
ATTRIBUTE.Explanation: This attribute should only be used if specimens cannot be split on an organ level (i.e. in situations where this information is only present on a case level without any mapping between anatomical sites and subsequent blocks).
